about: Sourced life stories for prophets-court (the prophets of the royal courts; Nathan and Asaph are written elsewhere). Written from Scripture and the dossier Research/People/prophets-court.md.

gad-1sa-22-5.short: A prophet called David's seer, who sent David from the hold into Judah, brought the LORD's three choices after the census, and named the place for an altar.

paragraphs.text: Gad first appears while David was in the hold, with his father and mother left in the care of the king of Moab. “The prophet Gad” told him to leave the hold and go into the land of Judah, and David went to the forest of Hareth.

Years later David numbered the people, and afterwards his heart smote him. The word of the LORD came to Gad, “David’s seer”, and he set three choices before the king: famine, three months of flight before his enemies, or three days of pestilence. Samuel gives the famine as seven years and Chronicles as three. David chose to fall into the hand of the LORD.

When the plague was stayed by the threshing floor of Araunah, Gad told David to rear an altar there, and David went up “according to the saying of Gad”. Chronicles says the angel of the LORD commanded Gad to give this word, and calls the owner Ornan.

Chronicles names “the book of Gad the seer” among the records of David's acts, and says that in Hezekiah's day the Levites served with their instruments by the commandment of David, of Gad and of Nathan. Scripture does not tell how Gad's life ended.

heman-1ch-6-33.short: A Levite of the Kohathites whom David set over the service of song, called the king's seer, whose sons were set apart to prophesy with instruments.

paragraphs.text: Heman was a Levite of the Kohathites, “the son of Joel, the son of Shemuel”, and his line runs back through Korah and Kohath to Levi. He was among those David set over the service of song.

When David gathered Israel to bring up the ark, the Levites appointed Heman, with Asaph and Ethan, to sound with cymbals of brass. Later Heman and Jeduthun served before the tabernacle of the LORD at Gibeon, with trumpets and cymbals, to give thanks to the LORD.

Chronicles calls him “the king’s seer in the words of God”. God gave him fourteen sons and three daughters, and his sons, with those of Asaph and Jeduthun, were set apart to “prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals”.

Singers “of Heman” stood at the dedication of the temple, sons of Heman served under Hezekiah, and at Josiah's passover the singers kept the order given by David, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun. Scripture does not tell of his death.

jeduthun-1ch-6-44.short: A Levite head of song in David's day who prophesied with a harp to give thanks; Chronicles calls him the king's seer.

paragraphs.text: Jeduthun served with Heman before the tabernacle of the LORD at Gibeon, with trumpets and cymbals, to give thanks to the LORD “because his mercy endureth for ever”. His sons were porters.
David and the captains of the host set apart his sons, with those of Asaph and Heman, for the service of song. Jeduthun himself “prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the LORD”.

Chronicles names “Jeduthun the king’s seer” at Josiah's passover. Some lists of David's singers name Heman, Asaph and Ethan; others name Heman, Asaph and Jeduthun. Scripture does not say whether Ethan and Jeduthun are one man. His name also stands in the titles of three psalms.

iddo-2ch-9-29.short: A seer named only in Chronicles, as the writer of visions against Jeroboam and of records for Solomon, Rehoboam and Abijah.

paragraphs.text: Iddo is known only as a writer. Chronicles says the acts of Solomon are written in “the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat”, those of Rehoboam in the book of Shemaiah and of Iddo “concerning genealogies”, and those of Abijah in “the story of the prophet Iddo”. Scripture records no word he spoke and tells nothing of his life.

ahijah-1ki-11-29.short: The prophet of Shiloh who told Jeroboam he would rule ten tribes, and later told Jeroboam's wife that their son would die.

paragraphs.text: Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam, Solomon's servant, alone in the field as Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem. Ahijah caught the new garment and tore it into twelve pieces, and told Jeroboam to take ten: the LORD would rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon and give him ten tribes.

He gave the reason: they had forsaken the LORD for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom. Solomon would keep the kingdom all his days, but it would be taken from his son; one tribe would stay with David's house, and if Jeroboam walked in the LORD's ways he would have “a sure house”. Solomon then sought to kill Jeroboam, who fled to Egypt.
Kings says that when Rehoboam would not hear the people, it was so that the LORD might perform the saying he had spoken by Ahijah.

When Jeroboam's son Abijah fell sick, Jeroboam sent his wife in disguise to Shiloh. Ahijah was old and could not see, but the LORD told him she was coming, and he greeted her: “Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam”. He told her the child would die when she entered the city, that Jeroboam's house would be cut off, and that Israel would be scattered beyond the river.

The child died as she came to the threshold of the door, and all Israel mourned him “according to the word of the LORD”, spoken by Ahijah. Later Baasha destroyed the whole house of Jeroboam, again according to Ahijah's word. Scripture does not tell of Ahijah's death.

shemaiah-1ki-12-22.short: A man of God in Rehoboam's days who stopped a war against the northern tribes and told the princes why Shishak had come against Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: When Rehoboam gathered a hundred and eighty thousand men of Judah and Benjamin to fight the northern tribes, the word of God came to Shemaiah, “the man of God”. He told them not to fight their brethren, “for this thing is from me”, and they went home.

Chronicles adds a second word. When Shishak king of Egypt took the fenced cities of Judah and came to Jerusalem, Shemaiah told Rehoboam and the princes that because they had forsaken the LORD he had left them in Shishak's hand. They humbled themselves, and the word came that they would not be destroyed, though they would serve Shishak.
Chronicles names “the book of Shemaiah the prophet” among the records of Rehoboam's acts. Nothing more is told of him.

azariah-2ch-15-1.short: A prophet on whom the Spirit of God came; he met King Asa, urged him to seek the LORD, and Asa put away the idols.

paragraphs.text: The Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded, and he went out to meet Asa. He told the king and all Judah and Benjamin that the LORD was with them while they were with him: “if ye seek him, he will be found of you”.

He spoke of a long season when Israel had been without the true God, without a teaching priest and without law, and of how the LORD was found when they turned to him in their trouble. He ended, “Be ye strong therefore”.
When Asa heard these words he took courage, put away the idols, renewed the altar of the LORD and gathered the people to a covenant to seek the LORD. Azariah is named only in this chapter.

oded-2ch-15-1.short: The father of the prophet Azariah; Chronicles also speaks of a prophecy of Oded the prophet that King Asa heard.

paragraphs.text: Oded is named twice. Azariah, on whom the Spirit of God came, was “the son of Oded”, and after Azariah's speech Chronicles says Asa heard “these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet” and took courage. No words of Oded are recorded, and nothing else is told of him.

hanani-1ki-16-1.short: A seer who rebuked King Asa for relying on the king of Syria, and whom Asa put in prison for it.

paragraphs.text: When Baasha of Israel built Ramah against Judah, Asa sent silver and gold from the house of the LORD to Ben-hadad king of Syria, and Ben-hadad turned his armies against the cities of Israel. Kings tells of this league too, but only Chronicles tells of Hanani.

Hanani the seer then came to Asa. Because Asa had relied on the king of Syria and not on the LORD, he said, the host of Syria had escaped him, though the LORD had delivered the Ethiopians and Lubims into his hand when he relied on him. “Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.”
Asa was angry with the seer and put him in a prison house. Scripture does not say what became of him. A prophet named Jehu is called “the son of Hanani”.

jehu-1ki-16-1.short: A prophet, the son of Hanani, who spoke against King Baasha of Israel and later rebuked King Jehoshaphat of Judah.

paragraphs.text: The word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha king of Israel. The LORD had raised Baasha “out of the dust”, but he had walked in the way of Jeroboam, and his house would be made like the house of Jeroboam.
After Baasha's death his son Elah was killed by Zimri, who destroyed all the house of Baasha “according to the word of the LORD, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet”.

Chronicles shows Jehu again when Jehoshaphat came home from Ramoth-gilead, where he had gone up with the king of Israel. Jehu went out to meet him and asked, “Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the LORD?” yet said there were good things found in him.
Chronicles says the acts of Jehoshaphat are written in “the book of Jehu the son of Hanani”. Scripture does not tell of his death.

jahaziel-2ch-20-14.short: A Levite of the sons of Asaph on whom the Spirit of the LORD came in Jehoshaphat's assembly, promising that the battle was God's.

paragraphs.text: When Moab, Ammon and others came against Jehoshaphat, the king proclaimed a fast and prayed before all Judah in the house of the LORD.

Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the congregation. He told them not to fear, “for the battle is not yours, but God’s”, said where the enemy would come up, and told them to “stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD”.
Chronicles goes on: the next day singers went out before the army, the LORD set ambushments, the attackers destroyed one another, and Judah gathered spoil for three days. Jahaziel is not named again.

eliezer-2ch-20-37.short: A man of Mareshah who prophesied against King Jehoshaphat for making ships with Ahaziah of Israel; the ships were broken.

paragraphs.text: Jehoshaphat joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel to make ships at Ezion-geber to go to Tarshish. Eliezer the son of Dodavah of Mareshah prophesied against him: “Because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the LORD hath broken thy works.” The ships were broken and could not go to Tarshish.
Kings tells of ships broken at Ezion-geber without naming Eliezer, and says Jehoshaphat would not let Ahaziah's servants go with his in the ships. Nothing more is told of Eliezer.

zechariah-2ch-24-20.short: A son of Jehoiada the priest, on whom the Spirit of God came; he warned Judah and was stoned in the temple court at King Joash's command.

paragraphs.text: Zechariah was the son of Jehoiada the priest. Jehoiada's wife had hidden the young Joash, and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him king; Joash did right all the days of Jehoiada.

After Jehoiada died, a hundred and thirty years old, the princes of Judah came to the king and he hearkened to them; they left the house of the LORD and served groves and idols. The LORD sent prophets to them, but they would not listen.

Then the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah. He stood above the people and said, “Why transgress ye the commandments of the LORD, that ye cannot prosper?” They conspired against him and stoned him in the court of the house of the LORD at the king's command. As he died he said, “The LORD look upon it, and require it.”

Chronicles says Joash did not remember the kindness Jehoiada had done him. At the end of the year the Syrians came against Judah, and Joash's own servants killed him “for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest”.

Matthew records Jesus speaking of the blood of “Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar”, and Luke of “Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple”. The Gospels do not say whether this is the son of Jehoiada.

zechariah-2ch-26-5.short: A man in King Uzziah's days who had understanding in the visions of God; Uzziah sought God in his days.

paragraphs.text: Chronicles says that Uzziah “sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper.” This one verse is all Scripture tells of him.

oded-2ch-28-9.short: A prophet of the LORD in Samaria who told Israel's army to send home the captives they had taken from Judah.

paragraphs.text: In the days of Ahaz, Pekah king of Israel killed a hundred and twenty thousand men of Judah in one day, and Israel carried two hundred thousand women, sons and daughters captive to Samaria.

Oded, “a prophet of the LORD”, went out before the army as it came to Samaria. He said the LORD had given Judah into their hand in his wrath, but they had slain them “in a rage that reacheth up unto heaven” and had sins of their own; they must send the captives back.

Certain heads of Ephraim also stood up against the returning soldiers, who left the captives and the spoil. The captives were clothed, fed and anointed, the feeble carried on asses, and all were brought to Jericho, to their brethren. Oded is named only here.

huldah-2ki-22-14.short: A prophetess in Jerusalem, wife of Shallum, whom King Josiah's men consulted about the book of the law found in the temple.

paragraphs.text: Huldah was the wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe, and lived in Jerusalem. When the book of the law was found in the house of the LORD and read to King Josiah, he tore his clothes and sent Hilkiah the priest and four others to enquire of the LORD, and they went to her.
She answered in the LORD's name: evil would come on “this place” and its people, because they had forsaken the LORD and burned incense to other gods.
For the king she had another word: because his heart was tender, and he had humbled himself and wept, he would be gathered to his grave in peace and would not see the evil.

Josiah then gathered the elders, read the book to the people in the house of the LORD and made a covenant. Chronicles tells the same events; where Kings has the evil come as “all the words of the book”, Chronicles has “all the curses that are written in the book”. Nothing more is said of Huldah.

uriah-jer-26-20.short: A prophet from Kirjath-jearim who prophesied as Jeremiah did; he fled to Egypt but was brought back and killed by King Jehoiakim.

paragraphs.text: Urijah the son of Shemaiah, of Kirjath-jearim, prophesied in the name of the LORD “against this city and against this land”, “according to all the words of Jeremiah”.

When Jehoiakim and his princes heard him, the king sought to kill him. Urijah was afraid and fled to Egypt, but Jehoiakim sent Elnathan the son of Achbor and others, who brought him back. The king killed him with the sword and threw his body into the graves of the common people.
The book of Jeremiah sets his story beside its account of how Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so that Jeremiah was not put to death.
